sentence: This project tries to find out which small molecules change the activity of a fusion protein that drives a fatal childhood cancer.
This project maintains a research resource of healthy rhesus monkeys of defined genetic and virological background for studies in the biomedical and behavioral sciences.
This project tests a simple way to prevent graft-vs-host disease after cell transplantation while keeping the effects that fight leukemia.
This project builds an inexpensive system that measures physiological responses to exercise in healthy adults and cardiac rehabilitation settings.
This project studies how small genetic changes called single-nucleotide variants help human T cells fight tumors in mice.
This project studies how neutrophils differ from one another and how their genes are controlled, using cells made from human induced pluripotent stem cells.
This project builds a toolkit that uses deep learning to handle every step of brain imaging analysis.
This project studies how environmental exposures lead to harmful outcomes and disease, especially at susceptible stages of life.
This project uses medical records and artificial intelligence to personalize advice on safely reducing or stopping sedating medications in older adults.
This project studies how a protein linked to muscular dystrophy turns on other genes and causes fibrosis and muscle degeneration in a mouse model.
This project studies how calcium signaling and central carbon metabolism are linked during capacitation in mouse sperm.
This project studies how RNA methylation changes an RNA binding protein and may drive neurodegeneration in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.
This project studies how neutrophils, a type of blood cell, and their precursors drive inflammation in coronary artery disease.
This project gathers evidence and develops practice recommendations on how germline variants are reinterpreted and reclassified in genomic medicine.
This project studies the brain-based and genetic mechanisms behind addiction, using genomics and neuroimaging data.
This project provides imaging, feeding studies and clinical research support for human studies of nutrition and obesity.
This project studies two signaling pathways to find out how the spine develops and what causes scoliosis, using genetic animal models.
This project studies how genetic mutations in a translation factor affect protein synthesis and brain development in human neurons.
This project measures tetrahydrocannabinol and endocannabinoid lipids in tissues and builds a highly sensitive method for measuring them.
This project studies risk factors and care for postpartum hemorrhage, using machine learning to improve how it is predicted and treated.
